definitions.explanation: A state of complete physical and mental exhaustion. A four-character compound (四字熟語) that emphasizes the extreme degree of tiredness, stronger than simply 疲労 alone.

examples.japanese: {疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい}で{動|うご}けない。
examples.english: I'm so exhausted I can't move.

examples.japanese: {三日間|みっかかん}{寝|ね}ずに{働|はたら}いて、{疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい}の{状態|じょうたい}だった。
examples.english: After working three days without sleep, I was in a state of total exhaustion.

examples.japanese: マラソンを{走|はし}り{終|お}えた{選手|せんしゅ}たちは{疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい}しながらも、{笑顔|えがお}でゴールした。
examples.english: The runners who finished the marathon crossed the goal line smiling despite their utter exhaustion.

notes:
USAGE:
A {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} (four-character compound). Can be used as a noun or with する. {疲労|ひろう} means fatigue; {困憊|こんぱい} means exhaustion/being worn out. Together they emphasize extreme, total exhaustion.
Stronger than {疲|つか}れた (tired) or even {疲労|ひろう} (fatigue) alone. Implies being completely drained of energy. Somewhat literary but commonly used when describing extreme tiredness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい}の{状態|じょうたい}: state of total exhaustion
- {疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい}する: to be utterly exhausted
- {疲労困憊|ひろうこんぱい}で{倒|たお}れる: to collapse from exhaustion
